messages:
Priya: :rotating_light: incident-bot alerted high fncall+structured-output error-rate on prod - visible spike in agent invocations. https://grafana.redwood/example
ops-bot: INCIDENT opened: INC-20240324-89 | severity: high | paged: @oncall-sre
Liam: seeing 3x baseline 1min tail latency, and many 500s from tool-runner pool. Likely cascade from agent-heavy tenants.
Chris: confirmed top tenants: tenant-42, tenant-ppc, tenant-alpha. tenant-42 accounts for ~48% of tool invocations.
Priya: immediate mitigation proposals: 1) global structured-output cutoff for >256 tokens 2) per-tenant soft quota for fncalls 3) enable fncall-guard feature flag (canary) — which do we want now?
Liam: prioritize opt 2 + 3. Soft quota can buy room without full feature removals. But if we can't slow down quickly, flip the structured-output cutoff.
Chris: I can push per-tenant rate limits via admin-api. Example:
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood/api/v1/tenants/tenant-42/limits \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"fncall_rate_per_min": 30, "structured_output_allowed":false}'
```
Chris: pushing soft cap 60/min for tenant-42 now (api request sent).
ops-bot: Task run: set-tenant-limit/tenant-42 - success (request id x7c9)
Liam: rolling out fncall-guard flag to 10% of traffic (canary). If stable for 2m, ramp to 50%.
Priya: also toggled global structured-output size limit to 256 tokens for the hot path (temporary). Command: `featurectl set structured_output.max_tokens=256 --scope=prod --note "incident mitigation"`
SRE Oncall: logs show immediate reduction in 500s after tenant cap + flag canary. tailing logs:
```
[14:03:12] tool-runner-3 ERROR invoke_timeout
[14:03:14] tool-runner-1 200 OK (fncall)
```
Priya: quick note — we need customer impact check: Liam, can you run a query for active requests that were truncated or had fncall disabled? Put results in incident doc.
Liam: running query... outputting to incident doc: https://confluence.redwood/incidents/INC-20240324-89
Chris: FYI, set quota ramp: tenant-42 60->30 if errors persist. We will roll back structured-output cutoff after 20m if stable.
Priya: Communications: ops-team to draft a status-page notification explaining degraded fncall/structured-output for a subset of customers. Not blaming customers, explaining mitigation.
Liam: draft posted in #customer-comms for review. pinged @marketing for signoff. :thumbsup:
Priya: Handoff plan: @SRE Oncall will stay on for next 30m, then hand to @Liam for monitoring. If error-rate < 1.5x baseline and latency < 200ms for 10m, start rollback steps.
SRE Oncall: I'm on it. Current actions:
- Monitor fncall error-rate dashboard
- Watch admin-api logs for limit hits
- Coordinate status page update
- Escalate to infra if GPU pools show OOM
SRE Oncall: adding postmortem template link and initial timeline to incident doc.
Chris: putting a temporary protective rule in the edge layer to reject requests that request function calls without allow_fncall=true header for untrusted tenants. Rule id: edge-protect-338
Priya: good. If we still see tail degradation after 45m, schedule capacity increase on dedicated pool (low-latency option) and prep CS for outreach.
Liam: metrics look green at the 12m mark. 500s down from 18%->3%. Keeping caps in place for 20 more minutes.
Priya: thanks team. I'll update the incident notes. If we hit regression, escalate to infra and re-open broader throttles.
SRE Oncall: handing to @Liam in 22m. Leaving a short summary in thread and incident doc. :wave:
Liam: taking over monitoring. thumbs up. :eyes:
